summary: This React component displays a helpful/not-helpful voting widget for documentation pages. It fetches vote counts from an API, lets users submit votes, stores their choice in local storage to prevent re-voting, and shows a thank-you message with updated counts after voting. The component carefully handles server-side rendering by deferring state initialization to the client side to avoid hydration mismatches.

explanations.18: This extracts the page path from the URL (removing leading and trailing slashes) to use as a unique identifier for tracking votes on this specific page.
explanations.20: A unique key is created for storing this page's vote in the browser's local storage, combining a prefix with the page path so different pages track votes separately.
explanations.22: Counts starts as null because the data hasn't been fetched yet; it will be populated once the API call completes.
explanations.26: The voted state deliberately starts as null instead of checking localStorage immediately—this prevents a mismatch between the server (which can't access localStorage) and client (which can), which would cause React to crash.
explanations.29: This effect runs after the component mounts on the client to safely read the user's previous vote from browser storage, updating the voted state if one exists.
explanations.38: If there's no page slug (meaning we couldn't extract a valid page identifier), we bail out early since we can't fetch votes for an unknown page.
explanations.40: The arrow function checks if the response succeeded; if not, it returns null instead of trying to parse failed responses as JSON.
explanations.47: useCallback memoizes this function so it only gets recreated when its dependencies change, preventing unnecessary re-renders of child components that receive it as a prop.
explanations.64: The vote is stored in local storage so that when the user returns to this page, the component knows they've already voted and can skip showing the voting buttons.
